analysis.session_summary: The session was dominated by a hawkish BOE: a unanimous 9-0-0 MPC vote against a 7-0-2 forecast drove GBP to close up 0.15%, with EUR/GBP falling 3.8 pips and GBP/USD up 11.1 pips. JPY and CHF led the G10, closing at their best at +0.436% and +0.377%, while AUD was the clear laggard at -0.857% with no catalyst of its own. USD first sold to -0.20% then recovered 72%, finishing only 0.067% stronger despite muted Unemployment Claims. VIX jumped 33.164% to 23.389, keeping risk conditions brittle.

themes.evidence: MPC 9-0-0 vs 7-0-2; GBP own impulse +0.152%; EUR/GBP sigma -9.33; GBP/USD +11.1 pips.
JPY +0.436%, CHF +0.377% both closed at best; AUD -0.857%, NZD -0.198%; VIX +33.164%.
USD sold to -0.20%, recovered 72%; Unemployment Claims muted 0.005%; DXY -0.05%.

currency_drivers.USD: Selling rejected after early -0.20%; no lasting US catalyst, recovered 72% despite muted claims.
currency_drivers.EUR: No own releases; followed cross flows and recovered with risk appetite, closing at session best.
currency_drivers.JPY: No own releases; broad safe-haven demand pinned it strongest, closing at its best.
currency_drivers.GBP: Hawkish 9-0-0 MPC vote against 7-0-2 forecast drove a persistent bid.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own catalyst; commodity/risk underperformance kept it weakest all day.
currency_drivers.CAD: Macklem was muted; early strength faded, giving back 90%.
currency_drivers.CHF: No clearly catalytic domestic news; safe-haven demand produced the second-strongest close.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own releases; attempt rejected, gave back 98% as risk appetite turned.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: The pair chopped in a 65-pip range: an early 49.0-pip rally and a 56.4-pip slide had no clear catalyst, leaving only a 4.3-pip net gain.

polarity_reads.event: MPC Official Bank Rate Votes +3 more
polarity_reads.read: A unanimous hawkish vote and GBP +0.152% impulse, EUR/GBP sigma -9.33, reveal heavy short-GBP positioning squeezed by the surprise.
Muted 0.001% own-currency move despite a 3.04 sigma USD/CAD push shows the market assigned no fresh CAD impulse, positioning already flat.
Beat with 189K vs 197K but 0.005% basket move means USD rates/labor data not the driver; positioning indifferent.
Muted 0.027% despite high impact; post-vote remarks added nothing, leaving GBP demand to the initial hawkish vote.
Muted 0.023% and weak CHF/JPY sigma -0.76 confirm CHF strength came from safe-haven flow, not the speech.

scenarios.name: Risk-on reversal / USD recovery
scenarios.thesis: Upcoming US NFP and UoM can support the dollar and stabilize risk appetite, allowing commodity FX to rebound from oversold levels while safe havens consolidate.
triggers: US Non-Farm Employment Change prints above 65K forecast
Average Hourly Earnings m/m meets 0.3% or higher

pair_paths.rationale: USD strength from firm US data reverses EUR/USD toward lower half of its 65.0 range.
Risk-on and US yields can lift USD/JPY from its 0.06 close-in-range; BOJ absent.
If risk stabilizes, AUD/USD can rebound from 0.04 close-in-range near its 76.1 range.

scenarios.thesis: VIX remains elevated and BOJ Ueda sounds hawkish, US data disappoints, keeping JPY/CHF supported and AUD/NZD pressured.
triggers: BOJ Gov Ueda Speaks hints at policy normalization
scenarios.invalidation: Strong US NFP and wages data break the safe-haven bid.

AUD already weakest -0.857%; risk-off extends decline.
CHF safe-haven bid extends; USD/CHF closed only 0.2 in range.
